docs.text: OpenFilter ¶ Layered navigation for Magento 2 and Hyvä. Free and MIT, built on the OpenSearch Magento already ships. Multi-select filters with correct counts : options of a filter you use are counted as if it were not set, in one search request. AJAX that Varnish can cache : a filter click fetches the same URL a normal page load would, so the page cache serves it; CSP-clean on Hyvä, no reload, back button and scroll restored. Works without JavaScript : every option is a real link, sliders are forms. Sliders and built-in filters : price (display currency and tax aware) and decimal sliders, rating, in stock, on sale, new. Mobile drawer with "Show 123 products" counted before you apply. SEO rules : readable URL names, one canonical URL per page (301), robots and canonical tags, nofollow and a limit on combined values. Admin with diagnostics : Filters grid, a form per filter, "Why is this filter not showing?", openfilter:doctor . Start with Install . Questions and bugs: GitHub issues (triaged within 7 days, no SLA).

docs.text: Admin ¶ Everything lives under Catalog › OpenFilter : Filters (one list of attribute filters and built-in filters) and Settings (Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter). Access is controlled by the ACL resources Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters and Stores › Settings › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter . First run ¶ After installing, the admin shows a notice: how many filterable attributes OpenFilter found and which defaults it set (colours as swatches, sizes as text swatches, price as a slider, other lists as checkbox lists, Yes/No attributes as switches). Rating, In stock, On sale and New start switched off. Review defaults opens the Filters grid and dismisses the notice. Set up OpenFilter (1.2) ¶ Above the Filters grid a checklist shows five steps and whether each is done, with a link to where it is done: review which filters show (the first-run notice's Review defaults ), put them in order ( Sort filters ), choose where filters show ( Settings › Display ), set the search engine rules ( Settings › SEO ), keep the OpenFilter and full page caches on. The states come from what was saved, so nothing is ticked by hand; Hide this list hides it for every admin user. A new install of 1.2 also starts with a useful order: category, price, the filters with swatches, then the other filters, each group in Magento's attribute order (written as sort positions, as Sort filters saves them). Shops that installed an earlier version keep their order. Filters grid ¶ One row per filter: label, code, type (attribute or built-in), how it looks, several values, options before "Show more", search box threshold, "Google may index", order (its place on the storefront: 1, 2, 3 …), position (the number behind the order), products must match (any / all), where it shows, storefront (shown or hidden). Above the grid, warnings name what shoppers would trip over: two active filters with the same name (rename one in Label and tooltip , or hide one), and search result pages without attribute filters. Inline edit : click a row, change the common fields, Save. Each row is saved on its own; a row with a value that does not fit (for example swatches on an attribute without swatches) reports its error and the other rows are still saved. Mass actions : Show on the storefront , Hide from the storefront , Show on search pages , Hide on search pages , Reset to defaults (labels per store view and URL names are kept). Hiding a filter never changes the attribute's own "Use in Layered Navigation" setting, so it stays in the grid. Show / Hide on search pages set the attribute's "Use in Search Results Layered Navigation" (built-in filters always show on search pages). Row actions: Edit and Why is it not showing? Sort filters (1.1) ¶ Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters › Sort filters lists every filter in its storefront order. Drag a filter by its handle, or use Move up / Move down (keyboard friendly: focus stays on the button and the new place is announced). Find a filter narrows the list by name; Save order stays at the bottom of the window and writes the positions 10, 20, 30… in one go (the gaps leave room for a filter later); the grid's Position column and the form show the same numbers. Filter form ¶ Section Settings Why is this filter not showing? the checks below, for any store view and category page How it looks display type: only the types that fit the attribute are offered (swatches need swatch data, sliders and ranges a number attribute or price, the on/off switch a Yes/No attribute or a list with two options, the category tree the category filter); Ranges (price and number filters, 1.1): a list such as 0-50,50-100,100- , empty = automatic; Category tree levels (category filter, 1.1): 1–5 How it behaves show on the storefront, several values, Products must match (option filters, 1.1): any of the picked values (more products) or all of them (fewer products, for features a product has several of), options before "Show more" (0 = all), search box from N options (0 = never), open when the page loads (automatic / open / closed), option order, hide when only one option is left, In the quick filter bar (1.2: its values may appear as links above the products), position (empty = the attribute's position) Where it shows (1.1) In every category (default), Only in these categories or In every category except these , with Magento's category picker; a category counts with the categories below it; search result pages always show the filter. Show only after a pick in (1.2): another filter this one waits for, and optionally Only for these values of it (empty = any value); filters that would wait for each other are refused Option images (1.2) an image per option for the Images display type (attributes with a list of options; edited with All Store Views ); remove an image to show the label again SEO "Let Google index pages filtered by this" (single-value pages only), URL name of the filter, URL names of the options Label and tooltip the label for all store views (empty = the attribute's label) and a tooltip (a short plain-text hint shoppers open next to the filter name, 1.1), or the chosen store view's own label and tooltip Saving is all or nothing: settings, labels and URL names are written in one transaction. One store view at a time ¶ The form edits one scope at a time, chosen with the store view switcher at the top of the page (the same switcher as on product and category pages), so it looks the same with 2 or 50 store views: All Store Views edits the settings (marked [GLOBAL] ), the label for all store views and the URL names for all store views. Reset to defaults is offered only here. A store view (for example Deutsch ) edits only that store view's label, the filter's URL name and the option URL names in that store view. The values for all store views are shown next to them, read only; settings are read only. Each option row also shows the option's label in that store view. An empty store view field shows Same as for all store views and follows the value for all store views. Clearing a field puts the store view back on the shared value. Save writes only the scope you are looking at and brings you back to it. Switching scope with unsaved changes asks first. To edit many store views in one go, use openfilter:config:export / openfilter:config:import ( Import and export ). URL names ¶ URL names are what shoppers and search engines see in filter URLs ( ?color=blue,red ). They are created once from the option labels and never change because a label changed (see Filter URLs ). Option URL names are checked as one set per store view before anything is written: lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, at most 64 characters, no name used twice. Two options can swap names in one save. A store view field left empty uses the name for all store views; a store view row is only stored where the name differs. This also holds for the filter's own URL name (for example farbe in a German store view instead of color ). Generate again from the label (per option) creates a fresh name from the option's label when you save: in All Store Views for every store view, in a store view only for that store view. This changes published URLs; old URLs with option IDs keep working, old names do not. Attribute page ¶ Stores › Attributes › Product › attribute › Storefront Properties has an OpenFilter fieldset for attributes that are filters: how it looks, several values, options before "Show more", search box threshold, URL name, "Let Google index". It is saved with the attribute (an invalid value stops the save). A link opens the full filter form for labels, option URL names and position. Saving any product attribute refreshes OpenFilter's cache, so an attribute that becomes filterable appears on the storefront without a cache flush. Landing pages (1.2) ¶ Catalog › OpenFilter › Landing pages (ACL Landing pages ) lists the pages with their URL key, category, number of filters, store views, robots value and status; mass action Delete . To make one, open the category on the storefront, pick the filters, copy the address and paste it into Filtered category page : OpenFilter reads the category and the filters from it (query or path URLs, the URL names of the page's first store view). When editing, the field shows the page's category and filters now; leave it empty to keep them. URL key is the address after the store's base URL ( black-tops , women/black-tops.html ); it must not be taken by a category, product or CMS page or by another landing page of the same store views. Heading and Meta title default to the title; Text above the products is HTML with widgets and variables. Saving cleans the OpenFilter cache and marks the full page cache invalid, as filter settings do. Insights (1.2) ¶ Catalog › OpenFilter › Insights (ACL Insights ) shows what shoppers do with the filters of one store view: see Insights . Apply to Sort filters opens Sort filters with the order by use, to check and save. Why is this filter not showing? ¶ The panel opens with one line (1.2): that the filter shows, or the first problem and its fix ("Not showing on search result pages" when only search pages miss it). All N checks unfolds every condition the filter needs, with what was found and how to fix it. The first problem is usually the answer. docs.text: Benchmark ¶ OpenFilter is measured against Magento's own layered navigation on the same store, with the same shopper scenarios, by a script anyone can run: bench/run.mjs in the dev environment ( node bench/run.mjs , or the E2E workflow with bench=true , which also fails when OpenFilter needs more engine requests than Magento or adds more than 15 ms). What is measured ¶ Measure How Search engine requests OpenSearch _nodes/stats query_total around one uncached page load Server time median of 11 uncached loads (Varnish and the page cache skipped), full HTML Page cache a scripted session of filter clicks; how many of a second shopper's pages Varnish answers OpenFilter's bytes its inline script and stylesheet on a filtered page, gzipped Magento runs with Hyvä's templates; scenarios use the URLs each mode understands (Magento: option ids, one value per filter) in their canonical spelling. Results ¶ Magento 2.4.9, Hyvä 1.4.2, OpenSearch 2, Luma sample data, Varnish; local Docker (Warden) on an Apple laptop, 2026-10-15. Absolute times depend on the machine; compare the columns. Scenario Magento: engine requests · server time OpenFilter: engine requests · server time Category page (Women › Tops) 4 · 189 ms 1 · 171 ms One filter (colour) 4 · 173 ms 1 · 171 ms Three filters (colour, size, price) 4 · 159 ms 1 · 160 ms Two values of one filter not possible 1 · 175 ms Search page 4 · 169 ms 1 · 160 ms Search with a filter 4 · 170 ms 1 · 165 ms Second shopper's clicks served by Varnish 5 of 5 6 of 6 OpenFilter's own bytes on a filtered page: script 6.0 KB, stylesheet 2.9 KB (gzipped). Lighthouse with OpenFilter on and off: same performance score (1.00), no layout shift added (the E2E workflow checks it on every run). What the numbers say: One search request per page, whatever is picked. Magento asks the engine four times per page (the products and its price intervals); OpenFilter gets products, every filter's counts (each without its own picks, so shoppers see what another value adds) and the slider bounds from one request. With the per attribute strategy (older engines) it adds one request per other active filter. No server time added , while doing more: several values per filter, disjunctive counts, built-in filters, SEO tags. Every filter click is a cacheable page. The AJAX layer fetches the same URL a browser would, so Varnish serves repeat clicks and the back button. The integration tests hold the same line on every Magento version in CI: 0 extra SQL queries and at most +15 ms server time per category page (measured −35 to −55 ms). Other modules ¶ Paid modules are not installed or measured (OpenFilter is written clean room). Their public pages, checked on 2026-10-15, publish no measured page times or engine request counts: Module What its public page says about speed Mirasvit Layered Navigation runs in production on catalogs of up to 600,000 SKUs; option counts are cached for up to an hour; "needs a properly sized server and a healthy OpenSearch instance to stay fast"; a changelog entry removes about 23 KB of JavaScript from pages with its widget Amasty Improved Layered Navigation describes AJAX filtering as faster; no measured numbers found (the page refused automated reading) Mageplaza Layered Navigation describes AJAX filtering as faster; no measured numbers found ElasticSuite replaces Magento's search stack; no layered navigation timings published If a vendor publishes measurements, open an issue and the table will link them.

docs.text: Facet counts ¶ Multi-select filters need disjunctive counts : with "Red" selected, the colour filter must still show how many products are blue, green or black, while every other filter counts only red products. Magento computes every aggregation under every active filter (conjunctive counts), so a multi-select colour filter would show 0 next to every other colour. OpenFilter fixes this behind one interface, Iranimij\OpenFilter\Api\FacetCountStrategyInterface , with two strategies. Strategies ¶ Strategy Code Search requests How SingleQuery (preferred) single_query same as core Active facet filters move from the query to post_filter (they still narrow the products), and each aggregation is wrapped in a filter aggregation that holds every active facet filter except the ones on its own attribute. One round trip. PerAttribute (fallback) per_attribute core + 1 per attribute with an active filter The main request stays as Magento builds it. For each attribute with an active filter, one extra request (no hits, only that attribute's aggregation) runs without that attribute's own filter. Setting: Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter › Search engine › How filter counts are computed ( openfilter/search/count_strategy ): Automatic (default), or a fixed strategy. Automatic uses SingleQuery on OpenSearch, Elasticsearch 8 and Elasticsearch 7, and PerAttribute for any other engine. Debug mode writes the choice to the log once per process. Which filters are "facet filters": term filters in the must part of the layered navigation requests ( catalog_view_container , quick_search_container ) whose attribute also has a term aggregation. The category drill-down ( category_ids ), visibility , price ranges and search text stay as Magento builds them. Other search requests (GraphQL, widgets) are not touched. Where it hooks in ¶ Verified on Magento 2.4.7-p10, 2.4.8-p5 and 2.4.9 (source of magento/module-elasticsearch 101.0.7-p5, 101.0.8 and 101.0.9, module-open-search 100.4.1–100.4.3, module-elasticsearch-8 101.0.x): Magento\OpenSearch\SearchAdapter\Mapper and Magento\Elasticsearch8\SearchAdapter\Mapper both delegate to Magento\Elasticsearch\ElasticAdapter\SearchAdapter\Mapper::buildQuery() , identical on all three versions. An after-plugin ( Plugin\Search\MapperPlugin ) collects the facet filters from the request, builds their clauses with Magento's own filter builder, and lets the strategy rewrite the query. Both adapters then call Magento\Elasticsearch\SearchAdapter\Aggregation\Builder::setQuery() and ::build($request, $rawResponse) , also identical on all three versions. Plugin\Search\AggregationBuilderPlugin hands build() the response with disjunctive counts (SingleQuery unwraps its filter aggregations; PerAttribute runs its count requests there), and hands setQuery() the original query, because core's price-interval data provider re-runs that query and must see exactly what core would have sent. Term filters with several values become a terms query in core already ( Filter\Builder\Term ), so addFieldToFilter('color', [49, 50]) is an OR within the attribute without further changes. Evidence (M0 spike) ¶ Test/Integration/Search/DisjunctiveCountsTest builds its own catalog (three filterable select attributes, 36 products in an anchor category, 4 outside it), then for each strategy and four selections (one value; two values of one attribute; two attributes; three attributes with multiple values) compares the counts of every attribute with brute force: one engine request per option, with OpenFilter switched off, counting products matching every active filter except the attribute's own plus that option. It also measures the requests each strategy adds over core on the engine itself ( _nodes/stats query_total ). Environment SingleQuery counts = brute force PerAttribute counts = brute force Requests added over core Run 2.4.9, PHP 8.3, OpenSearch 2.5 (local fixture) 4/4 selections, all attributes 4/4 SingleQuery 0 ; PerAttribute = active attributes (1, 1, 2, 3) local, 2026-10-13 2.4.9, PHP 8.3, OpenSearch 2.5 (local fixture), M1 catalog : simple + configurable products, 3 customer groups (Wholesale tier prices, price range), 2 store views (German view hides one product), category and search pages 4/4 scenarios, all 3 attributes; also equal to the catalog's own PHP model 4/4 — local, 2026-10-13 ( M1CountsTest ) 2.4.9 / 8.3, 8.4, OpenSearch 2.12 pending pending pending CI full matrix (after hours) 2.4.8-p5 / 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, OpenSearch 2.12 pending pending pending CI full matrix 2.4.7-p10 / 8.3, OpenSearch 2.12 pending pending pending CI full matrix 2.4.7-p10 / 8.2, Elasticsearch 8.17 pending pending pending CI full matrix Decision (preliminary, confirmed when the matrix is green): SingleQuery on every supported version and engine; PerAttribute stays as the automatic fallback for unknown engines and as a manual setting. If a matrix leg fails for SingleQuery only, that engine/version is mapped to PerAttribute in etc/di.xml ( autoByEngine ) and recorded here. Test note (M1): core's fulltext collection takes Api\Search\SearchCriteriaBuilder from ObjectManager::get() , one instance per process whose filters are never cleared, and the search indexer caches its attribute list per process. A storefront request builds one layer collection, so shops are not affected, but tests that build many collections or create attributes after an earlier reindex must reset those shared instances ( Test/Integration/Catalog/SearchIndexReset , and a fresh criteria builder per collection). The M0 brute-force test runs with that reset too. Sliders and the request budget (M1) ¶ Magento's price filter (and every decimal attribute filter) is a dynamic bucket: the main request already carries an extended_stats aggregation for it, but core's interval algorithm sends one or two more requests to build price ranges. OpenFilter's sliders need only min, max and count, so on layered requests Plugin\Search\DynamicBucketPlugin answers dynamic buckets from the main request's stats (bucket value stats ), and range filters on those fields are facet filters like any option filter: the price slider's bounds ignore the price range itself, but respect every other filter. Measured on the engine ( DisjunctiveCountsTest::testSearchRequestsPerPage , SlidersTest ): SingleQuery = 1 search request per category page (products, disjunctive counts, price and decimal bounds), PerAttribute = 1 + active attributes; core needs more for its price intervals alone. Bounds are converted to the display currency and tax display of the store view ( Model\Search\PriceBoundsConverter , default product tax class rate).

docs.text: Filters ¶ Settings ¶ Every filterable attribute and every built-in filter has settings ( Api\FilterConfigRepositoryInterface , Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters: see Admin ): display type, multi-select, options before "Show more", search box threshold, expanded, option order (position, name, count), hide a filter with one option, indexable for search engines, position, label per store view. On install OpenFilter stores sensible starting settings: colour-like (visual) swatches → swatch multi-select, text swatches → swatch multi-select, other selects → list multi-select, decimals → slider, Yes/No → toggle. Price and category are on; rating, in stock, on sale and new are off until switched on. Storefront requests read the settings and URL names from the OpenFilter cache type (Stores › Cache Management): no database query for them. Saving settings cleans that cache and marks the full page cache invalid. Behaviour ¶ Multi-select (OR within an attribute, AND across attributes) with disjunctive counts: options of an active filter are counted as if that filter were not set ( Facet counts ). "Products must match all of the picked values" (1.1) per option filter: for features a product has several of (a jacket that is Hooded and Full Zip ), the picked values combine with AND. Counts then say how many products have that value as well, so they shrink as values are added; the page still costs one search request. Options without products are hidden (Magento's "Filterable (with results)"), unless selected. A filter with a single option is hidden unless something is selected. Sliders (price, decimal attributes): bounds come from the same search request, ignore the slider's own range, and follow the customer group's prices; price bounds are shown in the display currency and tax display (default product tax class). Ranges (1.1) (price, decimal attributes, display type Ranges ): a list such as €0.00–€39.99, €40.00–€59.99, €60.00 and above. A range includes its lower bound and stops before the upper one. Your own list ( 0-40,40-60,60- ) or automatic ranges: about five, with round bounds (steps of 1, 2 or 5 × 10ⁿ) in the currency shoppers see. With "Shoppers can pick several values" on, picked ranges combine with any of ( ?price=0-40,60- ). Counts come from the same search request and ignore the price pick, like every other filter. Category: drill-down or tree (1.1). Checkbox list is Magento's drill-down (a link leaves for the subcategory). Category tree lists the categories below the page's category (the store's root on search pages) down to 1–5 levels with counts; picking one narrows the same page ( ?cat=21 ), several combine with any of ( ?cat=21,25 ) when "Shoppers can pick several values" is on. Counts come from the same search request and ignore the category picks. The tree is read from OpenFilter's cache (rebuilt when a category is saved, moved or deleted), so the page needs fewer SQL queries than Magento's drill-down. Option images (1.2) : for attributes without swatches (material, brand, style), the display type Images shows an image you upload per option in the filter form's Option images section, with the label and count next to it, like a swatch. Options without an image show their label. Images are the same in every store view, stored below pub/media/openfilter/options (JPG, PNG, GIF or WebP, up to 2 MB), read from OpenFilter's cache on the storefront and reported as swatch { type: "image" } in GraphQL. Dependent filters (1.2) : a filter can wait for a pick in another filter ( Where it shows › Show only after a pick in ), for example Size only after a Clothing type is picked, or Heel height only after Shoes . Optionally only for some of that filter's values. Until then the filter is not on the page, in GraphQL openfilter_aggregations or in the XML sitemap. Removing the parent's pick removes the dependent filter's picks too (also down a chain), so its URLs never keep picks of a filter that is not shown; old links with such picks redirect (301) to the page without them. Counts and the one search request are unchanged. Built-in filters : rating ("N stars and up"), in stock (only when out-of-stock products are displayed), on sale (per customer group and website), new ("Set Product as New" window, evaluated at request time). See Index fields . Coexistence ¶ When ElasticSuite or Adobe Live Search provides the layered navigation, OpenFilter switches its storefront part off and the admin shows a notice: never two filter systems on one page. Budget ¶ A category page with any number of active filters costs one search request with the SingleQuery strategy (products, counts, slider bounds, built-in counts) and no extra MySQL queries compared with Magento (measured in Test/Integration/Performance/BudgetTest ).

docs.text: GraphQL (headless) ¶ Headless storefronts (PWA Studio, Next.js, Vue Storefront, your own) get OpenFilter's layered navigation from Magento's products query: add the field openfilter_aggregations . query ($filter: ProductAttributeFilterInput) { products(filter: $filter, pageSize: 24) { total_count items { name sku } openfilter_aggregations { code filter_key label url_param display_mode multiselect logic tooltip position options { value label url_value count selected depth from to swatch { type value } } range { min max from to } } } } { "filter": { "category_id": { "eq": "21" }, "color": { "in": ["49", "50"] }, "size": { "eq": "167" } } } What you get ¶ The store view's filters (send the Store header) in the merchant's order, only where they show ( Where it shows , by the category_id or category_uid of the query), with the labels, tooltips and URL names of that store view. Counts that help shoppers pick: each filter is counted without its own picks, so with Black and Blue picked, Green still shows how many products it would add. Filters set to Products must match all of the picked values ( logic: "and" ) count with their picks. Values without products are left out unless picked. Picks: selected marks the values of the filter argument; value is what to send back ( filter_key names the argument: the attribute code, price , or category_id ). Sliders ( display_mode slider or from_to ): range.min / range.max of the products found without the slider's own pick, range.from / range.to the picked bounds. docs.text: The product list template ( Magento_Catalog::product/list.phtml ) renders section#product-list[tabindex=-1] containing the top toolbar, the grid ( .products.wrapper ) and the bottom toolbar (pager and limiter). It is identical in 1.4.2 and 1.5.2. Empty result: with no products the template prints only .message.info.empty ("We can't find products matching the selection") and no #product-list . OpenFilter's #of-results region must therefore wrap the product list block from layout, not live inside the list template. Sorter, limiter and view mode are not links: initToolbar…() builds the URL and sets location.href on change / click ( toolbar.phtml ). The AJAX layer intercepts these in the capture phase on #of-results : it reads the new value from the control, builds the URL from the current URL and stops the event before Hyvä's handler runs. The pager uses plain links. Region wrappers planned for M3: #of-filters (the leftnav block), #of-state (the state block, moved out of the filter block so chips sit above the results) and #of-results (a container around the product list block). Each region is a layout container ( htmlTag="div" htmlId="of-…" ).

docs.text: Hyvä ships Alpine 3.14.3 ( Hyva_Theme::js/alpine3.min.js ). It also ships alpine3-csp.min.js for strict CSP setups. Alpine.initTree(el) exists in 3.x and is what the AJAX layer calls on swapped regions after replaceChildren , so components inside product cards (add to cart, wishlist, swatches) start again. OpenFilter's component is written for both builds: x-data="openFilter" registered through Alpine.data , no inline expressions, and one inline script followed by $hyvaCsp->registerInlineScript() .
docs.title: Alpine

docs.text: Hyvä caches each product card for an hour. The key ( Hyva\Theme\ViewModel\ProductListItem::getItemCacheKeyInfo ) is: product id, view mode, template type, template, store, currency, the hide-details flags, the category id (only when categories are in product URLs), the customer group, the image display area, the image attributes and the tax rates. It contains no filter state . A filtered URL reuses cached cards, which is correct because a card does not change with the filters. OpenLabel's labels are part of the card HTML, so they survive every AJAX swap without integration code.

docs.text: Below the md breakpoint the whole filter block collapses behind the "Shop By" toggle ( blockOpen ) above the product list. There is no off-canvas drawer and no "Show N products" button, and every option click is a full page load. OpenFilter's drawer (M3) replaces this.

docs.text: Import and export ¶ Move filter settings, labels and URL names between installations (staging to production, one shop to the next) as JSON. bin/magento openfilter:config:export -o openfilter.json bin/magento openfilter:config:import openfilter.json --dry-run # lists every change, writes nothing bin/magento openfilter:config:import openfilter.json Format (schema 3) ¶ { "schema": 3, "filters": { "color": { "settings": {"display_mode": "swatch", "multiselect": true, "logic": "or", "visible_options": 6, "search_threshold": 12, "expanded": null, "sort_by": "position", "hide_single_option": true, "seo_indexable": true, "position_override": null, "active": true, "ranges": null, "tree_depth": 3, "depends_on": null, "depends_values": [], "quick_bar": true}, "labels": {"de": "Farbe"}, "tooltips": {"admin": "Pick one or more colours"}, "url_name": {"admin": "color"}, "options": {"Red": {"admin": "red", "de": "rot"}} }, "rating": {"settings": {"active": true}} } } Filters are keyed by attribute code or built-in code ( price , rating , stock , sale , new , category ); an attribute named like a built-in is attribute:<code> . Store views are keyed by store code; admin means all store views. Options are keyed by their admin label. When an attribute has several options with the same label, they are numbered in option order: "Wool #1" , "Wool #2" . Every section and setting is optional: a file may contain only what it changes. Schema 2 (OpenFilter 1.1) adds "logic": "and" ("Match all"), ranges (the list of the Ranges display type, for example "0-50,50-100,100-" ; null = automatic), tree_depth (levels of the category tree, 1–5), category_mode and category_ids ( Where it shows : all , only or except the listed category ids; ids are those of the store the file comes from) and the tooltips section. Files with schema 1 from OpenFilter 1.0 import unchanged. Schema 3 (OpenFilter 1.2) adds depends_on (the key of the filter this one waits for; null = always shown), depends_values (the values of that filter that show this one: option keys as above for an attribute, the built-in's values otherwise; [] = any pick) and quick_bar (the filter's options appear in the quick filter bar). Files with schema 1 and 2 import unchanged. All or nothing ¶ The import first checks the whole file: schema, known filters, store views and options, value types, URL name format. Then it writes every filter inside one database transaction through the same rules as the admin (display types that fit the attribute, URL names unique per attribute and store view). If any value is refused, nothing is written and the command lists the reason and exits with 1 . --dry-run runs the same checks and writes inside a transaction it always rolls back, so URL name collisions are found exactly as in a real import. OpenFilter's cache is cleaned afterwards; Magento may show "full page cache invalidated" as after any admin save. Over REST ¶ Integrations use the same document over Magento's REST API (admin token, or an integration with the OpenFilter › Filters resource): Call What it does GET /rest/V1/openfilter/config the document as a JSON string POST /rest/V1/openfilter/config with {"config": "<document>", "dryRun": true} checks and lists the changes ( applied , changes , errors ); "dryRun": false saves them, all or nothing GET /rest/V1/openfilter/filters?searchCriteria[...] the filters (search criteria on code , builtin , active , …) GET /rest/V1/openfilter/filters/:code one filter PUT /rest/V1/openfilter/filters/:code with {"config": {"sort_by": "name"}} changes the settings you send; the others stay. Read-only fields (code, attribute, label, position) cannot be sent. A value that does not fit the filter answers 400 with the reason; an unknown code 404 ; a call without the resource 401 .

docs.text: Index fields ¶ OpenFilter's built-in filters (rating, in stock, on sale, new) are filterable and countable in the search engine, so they need fields in the product search documents. M0 verified the core extension points on Magento 2.4.7, 2.4.8 and 2.4.9 ( Test/Integration/Index/IndexHooksTest , run on every matrix leg). Core registers categories and prices here. A provider implements AdditionalFieldsProviderInterface::getFields(array $productIds, $storeId) and returns fields per product id, batched. Declare the field types in the index mapping virtual type elasticsearch5FieldProvider ( Magento\Elasticsearch\Model\Adapter\FieldMapper\Product\CompositeFieldProvider ), argument providers (core: static , dynamic ) Used by the OpenSearch and Elasticsearch 8 mappers. OpenFilter adds one provider for of_rating (integer), of_in_stock (integer), of_on_sale_<group>_<website> (integer), of_news_from / of_news_to (date). What reindexes a product's search document ¶ The catalogsearch_fulltext mview subscribes to the product entity tables ( catalog_product_entity , _int , _decimal , _datetime , _varchar , _text ), category and website assignments, links, and catalogrule_product_price . Compared to "now" in the store timezone at query time, so no daily reindex is needed. none of_rating No : review_entity_summary is not subscribed. Plugin after review aggregation: reindex the product's search document. of_in_stock Not through the mview ( cataloginventory_stock_item is not subscribed). With MSI, Magento_InventoryCatalogSearch reindexes on salability changes ( UpdateFulltextIndexOnProductSalabilityChange ). Legacy stock: product save. docs.text: Insights (1.2) ¶ Insights show what shoppers do with your filters: which filters and values they use, which filters nobody uses, which filter combinations find no products, which filters are worth letting search engines index, and a filter order by use. They are off by default. Turn it on ¶ Stores › Configuration › OpenFilter › Insights : Setting Path Default Scope Collect filter insights openfilter/insights/enabled No store view Keep the counts for this many days openfilter/insights/retention_days 90 global With it on, filter pages (category pages, search results, landing pages, the All Products page) send a small report after they load and after each filter change. A cron job ( openfilter_insights_purge , nightly) deletes the days older than the retention, whether insights are on or off, so Magento's cron must run. The Insights page ¶ Catalog › OpenFilter › Insights (ACL Insights ). Pick a store view and a period (7, 30 or 90 days). Section What it shows Most used filters Filters by the pages they were used on, and their share of all filter pages viewed Most used values The 20 values picked most, with their store view labels Filters nobody used Active filters no page used in the period: hide them or move them down Filter combinations without products The 20 combinations shoppers asked for that found nothing: products to stock or tag Filters worth letting search engines index Option filters used on at least 10 % of the pages (and at least 20 times) that are not marked Let Google index pages filtered by this Suggested filter order Active filters by use, most used first; hidden filters keep their place at the end Apply to Sort filters opens Sort filters with the suggested order. Nothing is saved until you click Save order there. Below 50 page views the page says there is not enough data yet. What is sent ¶ One JSON body per page load and per filter change, sent with navigator.sendBeacon to POST /openfilter/insights/collect of the store view: {"s": "default", "c": 21, "f": {"color": ["49", "50"], "price": ["20-50"]}, "b": 2} Key Meaning s Store view code; it must be the store view the request reaches c Category ID, 0 on search results f Active filters: filter key (attribute code, price , rating , stock , sale , new , category ) and values (option IDs, ranges from-to , 1 for on/off filters, category IDs) b Products found, as a bucket: 0 none, 1 1–10, 2 11–100, 3 more, -1 unknown The endpoint answers 204 when it counted the beacon, 400 when anything does not match the store view (an unknown or inactive filter, a value no filter link could carry, more than 20 values, a body over 4 KB, another store view's code) and 404 where insights are off. It needs no form key, so pages from the full page cache can send it. Counts are added per day, store view, category, filter and value: one view, one count per filter, one per value (ranges count only as their filter) and, for a page without products, its filter combination. There is no row per request. Headless storefronts ¶ A headless storefront can send the same beacon: POST the JSON above to https://<store>/openfilter/insights/collect (with ___store=<code> where the store view is not in the address), after each products query with filters. Take the keys from openfilter_aggregations { code } and the values from options { value } ( GraphQL ); ranges as from-to . Send it only when insights are on for the store view; a 404 means they are off. Privacy ¶ Nothing about the shopper is sent or stored: no cookie, no customer or session ID, no IP address, no user agent, no referrer, no time of day (only the day). The script reads only the page ( #of-state and the product count) and sets no cookie or storage of its own. The endpoint reads only the body. Browsers send the cookies of the shop with any request to it, as with every other request of the page; OpenFilter does not read them, and Magento's visitor log skips the OpenFilter route. Counts cannot be traced back to a person, so no consent banner entry is needed for them under the usual reading of the GDPR; check with your own advisor if in doubt. Anyone can post a beacon, as anyone can load your pages: values are checked against your filters, so made-up values are refused, but counts can be inflated by bots that run JavaScript. bin/magento module:uninstall Iranimij_OpenFilter drops the table openfilter_insight_daily .

docs.text: Moving from another filter module (1.2) ¶ OpenFilter replaces a layered navigation module such as Amasty Improved Layered Navigation, Mirasvit Layered Navigation or Mageplaza Layered Navigation. Two things carry over: your filters, from Magento's own attribute settings, and the search engine value of the old filter URLs, through permanent redirects. Steps ¶ Install OpenFilter ( Install ) on a staging copy first. Run bin/magento openfilter:migrate . It lists the other filter modules that are still enabled, how many filters OpenFilter took over, and whether old filter URLs redirect. Switch the other module off with the command it prints ( bin/magento module:disable … , then bin/magento setup:upgrade ). Two layered navigations on one page break each other; openfilter:doctor warns while one is enabled. Review the filters under Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters . OpenFilter starts from Magento's attribute settings ( Use in Layered Navigation , position, swatches). The other module kept its own settings (display modes, SEO rules, option images) in its own tables; OpenFilter does not read them, so set what you need in the filter form. URL names come from the option labels ( Filter URLs ). If the old module had SEO-friendly filter URLs, turn on the redirects (below) and check a list of old URLs, for example the filtered pages Google Search Console reports: bin/magento openfilter:migrate --redirects=on --filter-keys=shopby bin/magento openfilter:migrate --urls=old-urls.txt # one URL per line: shows where each one redirects Redirects of old filter URLs ¶ Stores › Configuration › OpenFilter › Moving from another filter module › Redirect old filter URLs (off by default, per store view). When on, an address that no page has, starts with a category's URL and continues with filter words is answered with a permanent redirect (301) to OpenFilter's URL of the same category and filters, in the store's URL format (query or path ): Old URL Redirects to /women/tops-women/black-blue.html /women/tops-women.html?color=black,blue /women/tops-women/shopby/black.html /women/tops-women.html?color=black /women/tops-women/color_black.html /women/tops-women.html?color=black /women/tops-women/color/black-blue/size/xs.html /women/tops-women.html?color=black,blue&size=xs /women/tops-women/color:black,blue.html?price=20-50 /women/tops-women.html?color=black,blue&price=20-50 How the old path is read: The words after the category are matched against the store view's filters: each filter's attribute code and URL name, each option's URL name, written with dashes, underscores or nothing between their words ( heavy-duty , heavy_duty , heavyduty ), in any case. Options may be joined by - , _ , , or / ; an attribute name (or code) before options says which filter they belong to ( color_black , color-black-blue , color/black-blue , color:black,blue ). Path parts listed in Filter keys of the old URLs (default shopby ) are skipped. Query parameters stay; Magento's price parameter ( price=20-50 ) is OpenFilter's too. Nothing is guessed: if a word is unknown, or an option name belongs to two filters and no attribute name says which, the address stays a 404. Old URLs from a module that numbered duplicate names ( black-1 ) or used its own aliases need their own URL rewrites ( Marketing › URL Rewrites ), or matching URL names in OpenFilter's filter form. The redirect runs after Magento's URL rewrites, landing pages and the All Products page, so it never takes an address another page has. Addresses that begin with a route ( checkout/ , customer/ …) are not looked at; the others cost one URL rewrite query. The formats, and where they come from ¶ The formats were taken only from each vendor's public user guide (read on 2026-10-16); no vendor code was read or used. Formats a guide does not describe are not covered. Module What its guide documents Source Amasty Improved Layered Navigation option names after the category ( category/autumn.html ), joined by a chosen separator ( red-green-blue.html ); attribute code before the option ( color_black ); a filter key ( shopby/black-xl-activity ); price and decimal filters stay query parameters ( ?price=100-200 ) User guide Mirasvit Layered Navigation / SEO Filters short formats category/option1-option2 , category/option1/option2 , category/option1_option2 ; long formats category/attr1/option1-option2/attr2/option3 , category/attr1-option1-option2/attr2-option3 , category/attr1:option1,option2/attr2:option3 ; a filter prefix ( filterprefix/material/cotton.html ); multi-word attribute names without separator, with _ , - or capitals Filters SEO URL Mageplaza SEO-Friendly URL / Layered Navigation the option after the category ( jackets-women/heavyduty.html ); attribute code before it ( climate_allweather ); a filter key instead of the attribute ( shopby/allweather ) SEO-friendly URL Other modules whose old URLs follow one of these patterns are covered the same way.

docs.text: SEO rules ¶ Filtered category pages multiply: ten colours and six sizes already make hundreds of URLs. OpenFilter keeps search engines on the pages worth indexing and out of the rest. The rules are conservative by default: only pages you mark can be indexed. Robots ¶ Page Robots No filter your store's setting (unchanged) Exactly one value of a filter with Let Google index pages filtered by this your store's setting (unchanged) Anything else: two values, two filters, a filter not marked, a category drill-down plus a filter NOINDEX,FOLLOW Search results with any filter NOINDEX,FOLLOW Mark a filter in Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters › (filter) › SEO . Good candidates are filters whose single values match what people search for: brand, colour, material. FOLLOW stays everywhere, so crawlers still reach your products. Canonical ¶ Page Canonical Indexable filtered page the page itself: /women/tops.html?color=red (page number kept, sorting, limit and view mode dropped) Any other filtered page the category: /women/tops.html Search results none (as Magento) OpenFilter prints the canonical on filtered category pages even when Magento's "Use Canonical Link Meta Tag For Categories" is off, and replaces Magento's tag when it is on: there is always exactly one. Nofollow ¶ Once a page has 2 active values (setting: "Ask search engines not to follow filter links from this many active values"), the links that would add another value carry rel="nofollow" . Links that remove a value stay followable. 0 switches the rule off. Most values at once ¶ A URL with more than 5 active values ("Most filter values active at once") answers with a 302 to the URL with its first five values (in canonical order) and an X-Robots-Tag: noindex header. Bots that combine every filter end on a page that already exists, and your page cache does not fill with combinations nobody visits. 0 means no limit. Canonical parameters (301) ¶ Every filtered URL has one canonical spelling (filters in position order, values in option order, readable URL names, lower case). Other spellings, such as an old link with option ids, answer with a 301 to it; parameters in another order are left as they are (Magento's Varnish configuration sorts them) and name the canonical URL in their canonical tag. See Filter URLs . Title, description and H1 (1.1) ¶ Stores › Configuration › Catalog › OpenFilter › SEO has three templates for filtered category pages. Each is set per store view; empty keeps Magento's. Setting Example On /women/tops.html?color=red,blue Page title of filtered pages {filters} {category} \| {store} Red, Blue Tops \| Luma Meta description of filtered pages Shop {filters} {category} at {store}. Shop Red, Blue Tops at Luma. Heading (H1) of filtered pages {filters} {category} Red, Blue Tops {category} is the category name, {filters} the active values in the order of the page ("Red, Blue"), {store} the store name. Other text in braces stays as it is. Pages without filters, and search result pages, keep Magento's title, description and heading. Search results show about 60 characters of a title and 160 of a description; keep the templates short. Under each template the settings page shows a live preview (1.2) with a real category, two option labels and the store name of the default store view, and counts the preview's characters as you type. A title template does not change the heading; set the H1 template for that. XML sitemap (1.1) ¶ Turn on Add indexable filter pages under Stores › Configuration › Catalog › OpenFilter › XML sitemap , then generate the sitemap as usual ( Marketing › SEO & Search › Site Map , or Magento's cron). OpenFilter adds the pages its robots rule leaves indexable, and only those: one value of a filter marked Let Google index pages filtered by this (dropdown and multiple-select attributes), on each category page of the store view; only where the filter shows ( Where it shows ; a category counts with the categories below it); only with at least Only pages with at least this many products products (default 1), counted as shoppers see them; the pages with the most products first, up to Most filter pages per store view (default 5,000; 0 = no limit). Each URL is the canonical one ( /women/tops.html?color=red , the store view's URL names) with the categories' priority, change frequency and last modified date. Counting asks the search engine once per category, so a catalog with thousands of categories takes a little longer to generate. After AJAX updates ¶ Filter clicks fetch the same URL a crawler would and copy the title, meta description, robots, canonical and prev/next links from it, and the H1 when a heading template is set, so the page in the browser always carries the head a direct load of that URL has. Landing pages (1.2) ¶ A landing page has its own title, meta description, robots value ( INDEX,FOLLOW by default) and H1, and its URL is its canonical URL. The category page with the same filters names the landing page as canonical, and filter links that reach the same filters point to it, so search engines find one address per filter state. Landing pages set to INDEX are listed in the XML sitemap (with the categories' priority and change frequency), whether or not the filter page sitemap is on. Path URLs (1.2) ¶ Category pages can use path filter URLs ( /women/tops-women/color-black.html ), see Filter URLs . Robots, nofollow, canonical and sitemap rules are the same; canonical URLs and sitemap entries use the path form, and the other form redirects (301) to it.

Other spellings, such as an old link with option ids, answer with a 301 to it; parameters in another order are left as they are (Magento's Varnish configuration sorts them) and name the canonical URL in their canonical tag. See Filter URLs .
docs.title: Canonical parameters (301)

docs.text: Stores › Configuration › Catalog › OpenFilter › SEO has three templates for filtered category pages. Each is set per store view; empty keeps Magento's. Setting Example On /women/tops.html?color=red,blue Page title of filtered pages {filters} {category} \| {store} Red, Blue Tops \| Luma Meta description of filtered pages Shop {filters} {category} at {store}. Shop Red, Blue Tops at Luma. Heading (H1) of filtered pages {filters} {category} Red, Blue Tops {category} is the category name, {filters} the active values in the order of the page ("Red, Blue"), {store} the store name. Other text in braces stays as it is. Pages without filters, and search result pages, keep Magento's title, description and heading. Search results show about 60 characters of a title and 160 of a description; keep the templates short. Under each template the settings page shows a live preview (1.2) with a real category, two option labels and the store name of the default store view, and counts the preview's characters as you type. A title template does not change the heading; set the H1 template for that.
docs.title: Title, description and H1 (1.1)

docs.text: Turn on Add indexable filter pages under Stores › Configuration › Catalog › OpenFilter › XML sitemap , then generate the sitemap as usual ( Marketing › SEO & Search › Site Map , or Magento's cron). OpenFilter adds the pages its robots rule leaves indexable, and only those: one value of a filter marked Let Google index pages filtered by this (dropdown and multiple-select attributes), on each category page of the store view; only where the filter shows ( Where it shows ; a category counts with the categories below it); only with at least Only pages with at least this many products products (default 1), counted as shoppers see them; the pages with the most products first, up to Most filter pages per store view (default 5,000; 0 = no limit). Each URL is the canonical one ( /women/tops.html?color=red , the store view's URL names) with the categories' priority, change frequency and last modified date. Counting asks the search engine once per category, so a catalog with thousands of categories takes a little longer to generate.
docs.title: XML sitemap (1.1)

docs.text: Filter clicks fetch the same URL a crawler would and copy the title, meta description, robots, canonical and prev/next links from it, and the H1 when a heading template is set, so the page in the browser always carries the head a direct load of that URL has.
docs.title: After AJAX updates

docs.text: A landing page has its own title, meta description, robots value ( INDEX,FOLLOW by default) and H1, and its URL is its canonical URL. The category page with the same filters names the landing page as canonical, and filter links that reach the same filters point to it, so search engines find one address per filter state. Landing pages set to INDEX are listed in the XML sitemap (with the categories' priority and change frequency), whether or not the filter page sitemap is on.
docs.title: Landing pages (1.2)

docs.text: Category pages can use path filter URLs ( /women/tops-women/color-black.html ), see Filter URLs . Robots, nofollow, canonical and sitemap rules are the same; canonical URLs and sitemap entries use the path form, and the other form redirects (301) to it.
docs.title: Path URLs (1.2)

docs.text: Storefront (Hyvä) ¶ What shoppers get from iranimij/openfilter-hyva on Hyvä 1.4 and 1.5, how it behaves without JavaScript, and the markup contract themes can rely on from 1.0. What it looks like ¶ Filters in the sidebar, in the order of their position. The first three are open (setting Filters open by default ; per filter Open when the page loads ), the others are closed, and a filter with a selected value is always open. Each filter is a native disclosure ( <details> ), so it opens and closes without JavaScript and without moving the page. Options show their count. Options without products are hidden, except selected ones (so they can be removed). Lists longer than Options before "Show more" get a Show more (N) disclosure, and lists with more options than Search box from this many options get a search box that narrows the list as you type, including the options behind "Show more". Display types : lists with a check box, swatches (colour, image or text, always with a visible label and count), price and decimal sliders (two thumbs plus From / To fields), rating ("4 stars & up"), Yes/No switches (In stock, On sale, New and Yes/No attributes) and the category drill-down. Chips above the results: "Colour: Blue ×" removes one value, Clear all removes every filter and keeps the sort order. What happens on a click ¶ With Update results without reloading the page on ( Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter , the default), a click fetches the same URL a normal click would load, so Varnish and the full page cache answer it. OpenFilter then swaps three regions: the filters, the chips and the results (toolbar, products, pager). The previous results stay visible under a thin progress bar until the new ones arrive. A cached URL takes about 70 ms on the test store. The browser history gets the new URL. Back and Forward restore the filters and the scroll position. The page title, robots , canonical and prev / next tags match what a crawler sees on that URL. The focus stays on the option you clicked. After removing a chip, applying the drawer or changing the page, it moves to the results. A screen reader hears the new product count ("22 products"). Sorting, products per page, the grid/list switch and the pager use the same swap. If the response is not a normal page (an error or a timeout), the browser simply loads the URL. If a range or a typed URL leaves no products, the chips show No products match. Remove the last filter with a link back. Layouts and apply mode (1.1) ¶ Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter › Display (per store view; the defaults keep 1.0's behaviour): Bar above the products: the filters move above the chips and the results, the page uses one column (the sidebar's other blocks, such as compare and wish list, are left out on these pages), and every filter is a popover that starts closed. The filters take one row; the rest wait behind More filters (N) . One popover is open at a time; Escape or a click outside closes it. Phones open the same filters as the drawer. After "Show N products": on desktop, picks are staged like in the phone drawer: the filters update with their counts, a bar at the bottom of the window shows Show N products and Reset , and the results load once. Phones keep the drawer. Keep the sidebar in view: the sidebar stays next to the products while shoppers scroll ( --of-sticky-top ). It needs CSS :has() ; older browsers show a normal sidebar. The theme's sidebar spans the product rows while this is on; the second sidebar moves below it. Dropdown (per filter) is a native select in a GET form: without JavaScript its button sends it, with JavaScript a change loads the result in place. These parts load a small extra script ( js/extras.phtml , under 1.5 KB gzipped) only on store views that use one of them; the default page keeps the 6 KB budget. All Products page (1.2) ¶ With Stores › Configuration › OpenFilter › All Products page › Show the All Products page on, every product of the store view is listed with the filters at the URL key you choose (default all-products , also shop/all.html style). The page is the store's root category on Magento's category page, so the theme's category templates, OpenFilter's Hyvä templates, AJAX, robots and canonical rules and the SEO templates work as on any category page; it has its own title and H1 ( Page title and heading ), its URL as canonical, and an entry in the XML sitemap. The root category must be an anchor category (Magento's default root is). A page that already has the URL key (a category, a CMS page) keeps it. Landing pages (1.2) ¶ A landing page is a category with fixed filters at its own address, for example /black-tops for Women › Tops with Color: Black , with its own title, H1, meta description, robots value and a text above the products ( Catalog › OpenFilter › Landing pages , see Admin ). It is that category's page with those filters picked: the same templates, counts, chips, AJAX and toolbar, so shoppers can narrow it further; the other filter links start from the category's URL. The text is HTML with widgets and variables, as in CMS blocks. Filter links that lead to exactly a landing page's filters on its category (in any order) go to the landing page instead, and the filtered category page names it as canonical (see SEO ). A URL key that a category, product or CMS page already has is refused when saving; disabled pages and pages of other store views are not found (404). The pages are read from the OpenFilter cache: no SQL query on the storefront. More products (1.2) ¶ Stores › Configuration › OpenFilter › Display › More products chooses how shoppers see the next products: Magento's page links (default), a Load more products button after the list, or loading as shoppers scroll (two pages load on their own, then the button waits, so the page footer stays reachable). The button fetches the pager's next page (the same URL as the page link, so Varnish serves it), adds its products to the list, runs their scripts and takes over its pager; the live region announces how many products were added and the keyboard moves to the first new one. The page links stay for search engines and without JavaScript, the address does not change, and Back from a product loads the same pages again. The script (about 1.1 KB) is printed only on store views that use it. Quick filter bar (1.2) ¶ With Stores › Configuration › OpenFilter › Display › Quick filter bar above the products above 0, the values of the filters marked In the quick filter bar (filter form › How it behaves) show as one-click links above the products: picked values first, then the values with the most products, up to that number. They are ordinary filter links (they work without JavaScript and swap with it), with the filter's name for screen readers; on phones the row scrolls sideways. The bar is built from the page's own filters: no extra search request. Phones ¶ Below 768 px the filters move into a drawer, opened by a sticky Filter (N) button above the results (N counts the active values). Changes in the drawer are staged : the drawer's filters and counts update, and the footer button reads Show 123 products . The page behind does not change yet. Show N products applies the staged filters without another request (the page was already fetched to count N). Close , Escape , a tap outside or the Back button discard the staged changes; the focus returns to the Filter button. Touch targets are at least 44 px, swatches at least 36 px. Without JavaScript ¶ Every filter is a real link ( <a href> ) to the filtered URL, so crawlers and shoppers without JavaScript filter by navigation. The slider is a GET form with From / To fields and an Apply button (steps: Price slider step for prices); the store answers with a 301 to the canonical URL ( price_from=20&price_to=50 becomes price=20-50 ). On phones the filters show as a plain list. The search box and the slider's thumbs are not shown without JavaScript. Search results ¶ The search results page has the same filters, chips, drawer and swap. Every link keeps the search query ( q ). Accessibility ¶ Filters are disclosures; options are links with "selected" announced for selected values ( aria-current ); colour is never the only signal (label, check mark, bold weight). Slider thumbs: arrow keys move one step, Page Up / Page Down ten steps; the number fields are the accessible fallback. The drawer is a modal dialog (focus kept inside, Escape closes it). Automated checks: axe-core finds no WCAG 2.1 A/AA violation in OpenFilter's markup on load, after a swap, in the open drawer and on a right-to-left store view. Right to left ¶ The stylesheet uses logical properties only, so a store view with <html dir="rtl"> mirrors the filters: counts on the left, chips from the right, the slider's lower end on the right, the drawer from the right. Content Security Policy ¶ The AJAX component is one static inline script, registered with Hyvä's CSP helper ( $hyvaCsp->registerInlineScript() ), and works with Hyvä's standard and CSP Alpine builds. Templates print no inline styles or handlers; swatch colours are SVG fills. After a swap, inline scripts of product cards run once per distinct script, so a store with a hash-only CSP allows them when the first page carried the same script. Markup contract (from 1.0) ¶ Themes can style or extend these; class names and attributes stay stable within 1.x. Element Selector Filter region (swapped) #of-filters inside dialog#of-drawer.of-drawer Chips region (swapped) #of-state.of-state ( data-of-clear-url ; data-of-picks : the picked option ids per attribute code, {"color":["49"]} , for theme scripts that expect ids; [data-of-count-text] : the visible product count, filled by the AJAX layer) Results region (swapped) #of-results.of-results , ending with #of-count ( data-of-count , data-of-announce : the product count, printed after the product list) One filter details.of-group.of-group--{list,swatch,slider,from_to,rating,toggle,category,dropdown,ranges,tree}[data-of-group="<key>"] (the last three from 1.1) Option a.of-option / a.of-swatch with data-of-link , data-of-value , aria-current="true" when selected Show more details.of-more Search box .of-search input[data-of-search] Slider form.of-slider[data-of-slider] with [data-of-range] and [data-of-number] fields Chip / Clear all a.of-chip / a.of-clear Drawer button, footer button[data-of-drawer-open] , [data-of-drawer-apply] , [data-of-drawer-clear] Hint (1.1): "all must match", tooltip p.of-group__hint (with span.of-group__match ) at the top of .of-group__body ; next to "all must match" the tooltip sits in details.of-about ("About …") More filters (1.1, horizontal bar) button.of-more-filters[data-of-more-filters] ; filters beyond the first row get .of-group--overflow Dropdown (1.1) form.of-dropdown with select[data-of-dropdown-select] and button.of-dropdown__go (hidden once html.of-js is set) Category tree level (1.1) li.of-options__item--depth-{1..5} Horizontal bar, sticky sidebar (1.1) dialog.of-drawer--horizontal , dialog.of-drawer--sticky Desktop apply bar (1.1) [data-of-apply-bar] with [data-of-apply-show] and [data-of-apply-reset] More products (1.2) button.of-more-products after the product list; settings in #of-more-config[data-mode] Quick filter bar (1.2) nav.of-quick with a.of-quick__link[data-of-link] ( .of-quick__link--selected , aria-current ) at the top of #of-state Option images (1.2) the Images display type uses the swatch markup ( a.of-swatch with img.of-swatch__visual ) Any link with data-of-link inside the regions uses the swap. After every swap the window receives the event openfilter:swapped ( detail.url ); other components can listen to it. window.openFilter.navigate(url) swaps to a URL. Restyling ¶ view/base/web/css/openfilter.css (about 2.3 KB gzipped) uses only of-* classes and custom properties. Override the tokens on .of-drawer , .of-filters , .of-state or .of-results : Token Default Used for --of-accent #1d4ed8 selection, slider, focus ring, Apply, "Show more" --of-muted #6b7280 counts, captions --of-border #e5e7eb card borders, swatch frames, track --of-control #9ca3af checkbox frames, hover borders --of-surface #fff filter cards, drawer and button backgrounds --of-radius .375rem corners of controls --of-card-radius .5rem corners of the filter cards --of-gap .5rem spacing --of-row 2rem ( 2.75rem on touch screens) option row height --of-sticky-top 1rem distance of the sticky sidebar from the top (1.1; raise it under a sticky header) Templates can be overridden in a theme under Iranimij_OpenFilterHyva/templates/layer/... ( view.phtml , group.phtml , state.phtml , filter/{list,swatch,slider,rating,toggle,category}.phtml , js/openfilter.phtml ). Keep the region ids and the data-of-* attributes when you do. Switching it off ¶ With OpenFilter disabled, or stepping aside for another layered navigation (ElasticSuite, Live Search), the page keeps the theme's own templates: OpenFilter's layout handles are only added while it is enabled. With Update results without reloading the page off, the filters, chips and slider form stay and every click is a normal page load.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ A filter does not show ¶ Run bin/magento openfilter:doctor -f <attribute code> -c <category id> , or open the filter in Catalog › OpenFilter › Filters and use Why is this filter not showing? . Both list each condition with its fix: the filter is shown, the attribute is used in layered navigation (category and search pages separately), its field is in the search index, the category is an anchor, products in it have a value, and there is more than one option. Counts look wrong ¶ Counts come from the search engine. After bulk changes outside the admin, run bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogsearch_fulltext . OpenFilter's counts are disjunctive: the options of a filter you already use are counted as if that filter were not set, so "Blue 12" next to a selected "Red" means 12 products if you add blue. Log and debug mode ¶ OpenFilter writes to var/log/openfilter.log . Switch on Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter › General › Debug mode (it clears the full page cache) to get: log lines: the count strategy chosen for the search engine, why OpenFilter steps aside (another layered navigation), each request cut by the "most values" rule; attributes in the storefront markup, readable in the browser's inspector: Element Attributes #of-filters data-of-debug-strategy , data-of-debug-engine , data-of-debug-values (active values) each filter group data-of-debug-filter (filter key; "(core)" for Magento's own filters), data-of-debug-display each option link data-of-debug-option (option id or range), data-of-debug-count Keep debug mode off in production: the attributes are part of cached pages. Pages show old filters after a change ¶ Settings and URL names are cached in the openfilter cache type, cleaned on every save. The full page cache is marked invalid when a storefront setting changes; refresh it in System › Cache Management or with bin/magento cache:clean full_page . A theme changed the filter markup ¶ OpenFilter's templates can be overridden like any Hyvä template ( Iranimij_OpenFilterHyva/templates/... in your theme); keep the regions and data-of-* attributes listed in Storefront so AJAX updates keep working.

docs.text: Upgrade and uninstall ¶ Upgrade ¶ composer update iranimij/openfilter-hyva-bundle --with-dependencies bin/magento setup:upgrade bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy # production mode; in developer mode clean pub/static instead bin/magento cache:flush Deploy the static content after every update: the stylesheet keeps its URL until the static content version changes, so without a deploy returning shoppers keep the previous openfilter.css from their browser cache (new parts of the page would show unstyled). OpenFilter follows semantic versioning: Api/ interfaces, the URL format, the storefront markup contract ( Storefront ) and the CLI JSON format change only in a major version. See the CHANGELOG of each package. Switch off ¶ Stores › Configuration › Iranimij › OpenFilter › General › Enable OpenFilter = No per store view. Magento's own layered navigation (and Hyvä's templates) return at once; settings and URL names stay. Uninstall ¶ For a Composer install: bin/magento module:uninstall Iranimij_OpenFilterHyva Iranimij_OpenFilter bin/magento indexer:reindex catalogsearch_fulltext This removes the packages, OpenFilter's six tables ( openfilter_* ), its settings ( openfilter/* ) and the record of its data patches, so a later install starts with fresh defaults. Keep the export of your settings first: bin/magento openfilter:config:export -o openfilter.json . The reindex removes OpenFilter's fields from the product search index. Magento's attributes and their "Use in Layered Navigation" flags are never changed by OpenFilter; "Use in Search Results Layered Navigation" changes only when you use the grid's Show on search pages / Hide on search pages . iranimij/module-base stays installed while other iranimij modules use it.

docs.text: Filter URLs ¶ OpenFilter keeps Magento's routing and URL rewrites: filters are query parameters on the normal category or search URL, with readable, store-scoped names. /women/tops-women.html?color=blue,red&size=m&price=20-80&rating=4&stock=1 Filter Parameter Value Attribute (list, swatch) the attribute's URL name (default: its code) option URL names, comma-separated ( %2C works too) Price, decimal attributes price , the attribute's URL name min-max with . as decimal separator; open ends 20- and -80 ; price in the display currency Rating rating 4 = 4 stars and up (1–5) In stock, on sale, new stock , sale , new 1 Category Magento's own ( cat on search pages, the category URL on category pages) URL names ¶ Option URL names are generated once from the option labels: lower case, German transliteration first (Grün → gruen , Weiß → weiss ), any other script to ASCII, everything else becomes - . Collisions within one attribute and store view get -2 , -3 in option order. Store views get their own name only where it differs (German rot next to red ). Names never change because a label changed, so published URLs stay valid. New options get a name when the attribute is saved. Parameter names avoid Magento's own ( p , q , cat , product_list_* , ___store ) and the built-in filters ( price , rating , stock , sale , new ): Luma's sample attributes new and sale become new-2 and sale-2 . Old links keep working: a numeric option id is accepted in place of its name. Canonical URLs (301) ¶ Every filter URL has one canonical form: filters in position order, values in option order, URL names, lower case, no duplicates or unknown values. Category and search pages answer other forms with a 301 to the canonical URL, except when only the order of the parameters differs (Magento's Varnish configuration sorts query parameters before Magento sees them, so a redirect for the order would loop; the canonical tag names the one URL); sort order, limit and view mode stay, the page number resets only when values were dropped. Other parameters (tracking, for example) may sit anywhere. POST requests are never redirected. Links OpenFilter renders are canonical already, so shoppers and crawlers never hit the redirect; it catches hand-written, old and external links and keeps one cache entry per filtered page. Path URLs (1.2, opt-in) ¶ Stores › Configuration › OpenFilter › SEO › Filter URLs on category pages = Paths writes the filters of category pages as path segments instead of query parameters: /women/tops-women.html?color=black,blue&size=m → /women/tops-women/color-black,blue/size-m.html One segment per filter, <URL name of the filter>-<values> , values comma-separated as in the query format, filters in position order, then the category URL suffix. Ranges keep their format: price-10-50 , price--50 , price-100- . Page number, sort order and view mode stay in the query: /women/tops-women/color-black.html?p=2 . A filter whose segment could read as another filter (a URL name that starts with another one plus a dash) stays in the query, so every URL reads back to the same filters. Query links (old links, the no-JavaScript slider and dropdown forms) and segments in another order answer with a 301 to the canonical path. Switching back to query parameters redirects path links the same way. Search result pages and the All Products page keep query parameters; category URLs without a URL rewrite ( catalog/category/view/id/12 ) too. The path is resolved before Magento's URL rewrite router, from cached settings: no extra SQL query, one search request as before. Canonical tags, the XML sitemap and every link follow the format. Reading and writing URLs in code ¶ Iranimij\OpenFilter\Api\UrlCodecInterface turns parameters into an Api\FilterStateInterface ( decode ) and back ( encode , urlFor ; the query format). Model\Url\PathUrl builds and reads the path format. Unknown parameters are ignored, values are checked against the attribute's options, numbers are clamped (price ≥ 0, ≤ 10⁹; rating 1–5).
